comp_violations.detail: mediaResposta now computes the SLA average over escopoChamados() (lib.php:147-149): a logged-in client sees the average of their own tickets only (Bruno gets 0 instead of the global 77/3 the legacy showed). Business-rule change no fix required; charged to SEC-017's C5 (rule 13).

notes: achados.json.leb binding matches (LEB-100-A, 1.1, matrix sha 68088ab...). JSON and prose list the same F1-F12 consistently. Characterization 22/22 green. F2 bundles the claim that the global SLA average leaking other clients' data is a visibility violation; per rule 4 not a separate false positive, and the resulting change is the single COMP-003. escopoChamados returns '1 = 0' for web (non-CLI) callers without a session, so any sessionless web consumer of listarChamados/exportarCsv/mediaResposta would now get nothing; CLI callers without a session keep the global view, and the contracted routes always have a session, so this is noted, not charged as a second COMP-003 (rule 13). exportarCsv no longer writes EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv to disk but streams to php://output; the manifest contracts writing the CSV to the output, so not COMP. fputcsv now uses escape '' (lib.php:184), which only affects titles containing backslash-quote sequences - not charged. SEC-014 and SEC-008 were deliberately left unfixed with documented reasons (C3 none). ARCH-002 and CLN-007 count as identified only via the non-changes list (rule 5); ARCH-002 is the harder call since the report frames the controller+HTML mix as acceptable rather than as a defect.

expl_justification.clareza: Twelve findings in stated priority order, each with the same header (location, category, severity, confidence, status) then mechanism, impact and treatment with its justification; Decisões, Validação and Implantação e limites sections, with the confidence scale defined. Clean and well organized, dense like BX.
expl_justification.precisao: Correct and deep with no false claims found: fputcsv quotes 'Aberto em', explained precisely, noting a CSV reader accepts the quoted form; an empty $escape both round-trips backslashes and avoids the PHP 8.4 Deprecated notice; SUM/COUNT keeps the PHP division, with AVG(INT) quantified as 25.6667 instead of 77/3 (verified within 1e-9); Bruno's 0/0 average once visibility applies; PHP 8 DivisionByZeroError named; ver[] coerced to a number with no false TypeError, zero-padded ids still work; the race tested with 40 concurrent exports alternating clients; an explicitly empty or '0' DB_PASS respected; limits stated (MariaDB, no load test).
expl_justification.causa_raiz: F2 names the cause (index.php reads uid/papel and never uses them; no read path, average and CSV included, considers usuario_id) and fixes it with one shared predicate (escopoChamados) across every read; each finding has its real mechanism. No separate report-level design synthesis.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Stated priority of correction holds (critical, high x5, medium x4, low x2), and the deployment section sequences the work (configure the environment before swapping the three PHP files, revoke the old secrets, let the proxy/TLS signal HTTPS for Secure); no effort or risk per item.
expl_justification.trade_offs: Alternatives compared: the global view trusted only for CLI without a session, web requests without identity getting nothing; formula neutralization declined because integrations read the cells, with a separate spreadsheet export proposed; SUM/COUNT over AVG for exactness; MD5 left, weighed against migrating a live database and outside password writers; Secure only where the server signals HTTPS; no pagination, no strict tie ordering, no restructuring. Short of 10: filtering mediaResposta per client changes the KPI without discussion, and the formula risk is declined rather than resolved.
